name: Infiniti Q50 3.0t
reliability: 6/10 — strong engine, but turbo complexity and wastegate rattle at mileage
cost_to_own: Insurance: Moderate-High (turbo luxury sedan) · Maintenance ~$700/yr (premium fuel)
popular_mods: Ecutek tune or JB4 piggyback (+40-100 whp → 350-400 whp)
Catless downpipes, cold air intakes, upgraded intercoolers (FBO ~440-475 whp)
E85 flex fuel + upgraded HPFP/LPFP (500+ whp on stock turbos)
Huge tuning headroom — one of the best bang-for-buck platforms out there
oil_interval: Every 5,000 miles (recommended — do not stretch intervals on a turbo)

generations.2016–2017 (VR30 Introduction): 3.7L replaced by 3.0L twin-turbo VR30DDTT. 300hp and 400hp (Red Sport) variants introduced. 2nd-gen Direct Adaptive Steering.
generations.2018–2023 (Refresh): Visual refresh unveiled at 2017 Geneva Motor Show. Improved interior quality, clearer trim levels, added driver-assistance tech. Base 2.0T four-cylinder added.
generations.2024 (Final Year): Infiniti announced discontinuation in August 2024. Last model year for US and Canada after 11 years. Slow sales ended the run.

common_issues: Wastegate rattle — pivot point wears inside turbo housing
Valve body issues and rear differential bushing wear at high mileage
Oil consumption if intervals are extended
maintenance_tips: Do not extend oil changes past 5,000 miles — turbos are oil-dependent
Change transmission fluid every 30-40k miles (Infiniti says lifetime — ignore that)
Monitor coolant level — turbocharged engines are harder on cooling systems

engine.detail: 3.0L VR30DDTT twin-turbo 60-degree V6 — 300 hp and 295 lb-ft, direct-injected, with a Garrett turbo per cylinder bank running roughly 9.5 psi through a water-to-air intercooler. Strong and heavily tunable.
engine.watch: Wastegate rattle — the pivot point wears inside the turbo housing and produces a signature idle/low-load rattle at mileage. And it will consume oil if you stretch intervals: keep to 5k, no exceptions, because the turbos live on that oil.

drivetrain.detail: Jatco 7-speed automatic (JR711E), rear-drive or Intelligent AWD.
drivetrain.watch: Valve-body issues and rear differential bushing wear show up at higher mileage. Change the transmission fluid every 30-40k despite Infiniti's 'lifetime' spec.

suspension.detail: Double-wishbone front, multi-link rear, with Infiniti's 2nd-gen Direct Adaptive Steering (steer-by-wire) available.
suspension.watch: DAS steering feels numb and disconnected — the common gripe across the range. Refresh bushings and dampers on older cars; coilovers and sway bars are the go-to.

brakes.detail: Vented front discs with ABS and stability control.
brakes.watch: Adequate for the street; upgraded pads and fresh fluid are all a spirited driver needs.

body.detail: Steel unibody four-door at about 3,820 lbs.
body.watch: Turbocharged engines run the cooling system harder — keep an eye on coolant level and hose condition; otherwise standard age-related trim and paint wear.
